citation: David Loker, CodeRabbit. 'State of AI vs Human Code Generation Report' (blog post titled 'Our new report: AI code creates 1.7x more problems'). CodeRabbit blog, 17 December 2025. https://coderabbit.ai/blog/state-of-ai-vs-human-code-generation-report
access_status: Blog post fetched and read via a summarising fetch tool; full whitepaper methodology not opened [uncertain]
sponsor_and_incentive: CodeRabbit conducted the study and sells an AI code review product. The post promotes it ('An AI code review tool like CodeRabbit', 'Try CodeRabbit today', free-trial calls to action). Findings that AI code has more issues directly support the product's value proposition.
exact_quotes: Intro: "AI accelerates output, but it also amplifies certain categories of mistakes." | Top 10 findings: "No issue category was uniquely AI but most categories saw significantly more errors in AI-authored PRs." | Body: "AI-authored changes produced 10.83 issues per PR, compared to 6.45 for human-only PRs." | Limitations: "we cannot guarantee all the PRs we labelled as human authored were actually authored only by humans." | Bottom line: "Quality isn't automatic. It requires deliberate engineering. Even when using AI tools." | Bottom line: "An AI code review tool could also help." [quotes taken from fetch-tool output, not a raw page copy; uncertain]
date_and_recency: Published 17 December 2025. Data collection window not stated in the post.
key_claims: AI co-authored PRs had about 1.7x more issues overall than human-only PRs. Critical and major findings about 1.4 to 1.7x. Logic and correctness 75% more common. Readability more than 3x (largest difference). Error handling nearly 2x. Security up to 2.74x. Excessive I/O about 8x (small in number). Concurrency and dependency correctness about 2x. Formatting 2.66x. Naming nearly 2x. No category was uniquely AI.
headline_figures: 10.83 issues per PR (AI-authored) vs 6.45 (human-only); ratio about 1.68, reported as ~1.7x. Post's body states these as 'per PR'. Methodology text says findings were 'normalized to issues per 100 PRs'. Category figures are given only as ratios (1.4-1.7x, 1.75x, >3x, ~2x, up to 2.74x, ~8x, 2.66x). Window: not stated.
sample_unit_and_population: 470 open-source GitHub pull requests: 320 AI co-authored, 150 human-only. Unit is the PR. AI status inferred from co-authorship signals; PRs without signals treated as human.
observed_vs_stated: Observed: findings counted on real PRs using CodeRabbit's issue taxonomy (the findings are produced by CodeRabbit's own review tool [uncertain]). Authorship label is inferred, not confirmed.
what_makes_trust_justified: Deliberate engineering: the post says quality is not automatic and recommends review gates on every PR, plus AI code review tooling (CodeRabbit) to standardise review and reduce reviewer workload.
what_it_costs: Not quantified. Implied cost is added review burden on human reviewers (post argues tooling reduces it) and the tool subscription.
failure_mode_class: Wrong code (logic, correctness, error handling), security issues, readability and maintainability, over-reliance.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Post suggests review gates and AI-assisted review on every PR.
limitations_stated: Authorship could not be confirmed per PR; 'we cannot guarantee all the PRs we labelled as human authored were actually authored only by humans.' Differences described as statistically significant but dependent on that classification. Full methodology deferred to the whitepaper.
counter_evidence: Vendor conflict of interest. Unequal group sizes (320 vs 150) and unstated time window. Issue counts come from an AI reviewer that also sells the fix, so detection bias is possible. Human group may contain undetected AI use, and AI PRs may differ in size or type (not controlled in the post as read) [uncertain]. Issue counts are not severity-weighted outcomes such as production bugs.
verification_status: Sample size 470 (320/150), 10.83 vs 6.45, 1.7x: checked against the blog post as read via fetch tool. Per-PR vs per-100-PR wording: NOT resolved against the whitepaper, which was not opened [uncertain]. Cortex benchmark figure in post is secondhand and unverified.
usable_claim: In CodeRabbit's December 2025 analysis of 470 open-source PRs, the 320 AI co-authored PRs averaged 10.83 issues per PR against 6.45 for 150 human-only PRs, about 1.7x. CodeRabbit sells AI code review, and authorship was inferred from co-authorship signals.
do_not_use: Do not quote 10.83 or 6.45 as 'per 100 PRs' (the post wording is per PR; a 6.45 per 100 PRs reading would be implausible, but confirm against the whitepaper). Do not present category multipliers (8x I/O, 2.74x security) as general facts; do not call it independent or peer-reviewed. Do not state a collection window.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Unknown; not checked against the Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays [uncertain].
